extracted.intended_audience: lawyers, judges, and legal scholars arguing or deciding injunctions and misappropriation claims between news agencies and competitors
extracted.subtask_description: Legal-argument brief addressing when equity may protect a news-gathering enterprise from commercial appropriation of its news (seeking injunctions against rival distributors). Focuses on common-law property in news, implied restrictions on publication and use, and analogies to trademarks and other intangible business assets.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equitable protection when symbol/speech used commercially
rubrics_metrics.description: Standing apart, the symbol or speech is not property. Disconnected from the business in which it is utilized it cannot be monopolized. But used as a method of making an enterprise succeed, so that its appropriation by another would be a distinctive injury to the enterprise to which it is attached, the name, or mark, becomes at once the subject-matter of equitable protection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Equity protects names/marks/speech not in the abstract but when they operate as a commercial method of making an enterprise succeed and their appropriation would injure that enterprise. The injunction may act not on the mere thing but on acts that will result, even remotely, in injury to property.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equity may enjoin acts that remotely injure property
rubrics_metrics.description: Here, as elsewhere, the eye of equity jurisdiction seeks out results, and though the immediate thing to be acted upon by the injunction is not itself, alone considered, property, it is enough that the act complained of will result even though somewhat remotely in injury to the property.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Courts can restrain conduct that indirectly or consequentially diminishes enjoyment or value of property rights when legal remedies are inadequate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ticker/news as implement; protection against appropriation that injures service
rubrics_metrics.description: The business of appellee is that of a carrier of information. The gist of its service to the patron is that, by such carriage, the patron acquires knowledge of the matter communicated earlier than those not thus served. The ticker, with its printed tape, is an implement or means only to this commercial end... but may not appropriate to some end not intended, especially if such appropriation result in injury to, or total destruction of, the service.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Protection is aimed at preventing rivals from appropriating the producer's means of delivering time-sensitive commercial value (e.g., news) for competing business purposes that injure the original service.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duration of protection tied to commercial utility/publication window
rubrics_metrics.description: Upon the facts of the commercial conditions of this particular business, the period necessary for effective protection of the complainant's rights in these news values created by it, is whatever period is necessary to afford opportunity for such complete country-wide publication as to enable every member to realize the full value of the news.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The appropriate protection period is pragmatic — long enough to allow the originator to secure the commercial value of a dispatch (e.g., country-wide publication), not an arbitrary fixed statutory term.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on rivals making business use of taken news
rubrics_metrics.description: There would hardly be any time when a rival news distributing company like the defendant could lawfully make business use of the complainant's news — meaning by this, not that it could never publish the particular fact as news, but only that it cannot take it from us for that purpose, and that so long as our message has any business value (as news) which would make it usable by defendant, it belongs to us.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rivals may report the same facts independently, but may not appropriate the plaintiff's collected/distributed news for commercial use that exploits the plaintiff's investment and timing advantage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinction between news and analytical reviews (no competition)
rubrics_metrics.description: The definitive characteristic of news, as a commercial product, is its newness, whereas the definitive characteristic of the reviews is their summarization, analysis, and criticism. The businesses are in totally different fields and do not compete.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Shows scope of protection: activities that merely analyze or comment do not compete with time-sensitive news distribution, so the misappropriation claim focuses on competitors using news as a commercial product.

rubrics_metrics.name: Analogy to trademarks and surviving property right for commercial utility
rubrics_metrics.description: They involve the use of words, generally in combination... but nevertheless the property right which they represent survives for the whole period of their commercial utility to their producer. Precisely like news, as a commercial commodity, their only usefulness to their owner is in their widespread and complete publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Intangible commercial rights (like trademarks) can survive publication so long as they retain commercial utility; courts may treat news similarly when widespread publication is precisely how value is realized.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protection against illegitimate use by purchasers
rubrics_metrics.description: Just as the court conceded the right of the defendant to buy phonograph records and use them for any legitimate purpose, but denied the right to use them illegitimately in violation of complainant's rights... defendant can use complainant's news for all legitimate purposes but not in violation of complainant's rights.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sale or transfer of a physical item does not necessarily authorize purchasers to use it in ways that infringe the seller's residual intangible business rights; courts may enjoin such misuse.

rubrics_metrics.name: Intangible business qualities are property and protectable
rubrics_metrics.description: The great value of complainant's business lies in the interchangeability of its tanks. This quality the complainant has created. It is his, and no one has the right to appropriate it for his own gain to the detriment and even destruction of complainant's business. That quality is incorporeal and intangible, but is property nevertheless.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Courts will recognize and protect intangible/systemic business advantages (e.g., service systems, reputation, interchangeability) where appropriation would destroy the business.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fair competition does not include appropriating a competitor's valuable system
rubrics_metrics.description: Fair competition between the two systems is excellent, but the acts complained of do not involve competition between the two systems. They involve a use by the defendants in the furtherance of their competitive business, and the appropriation, of something of value which actually belongs to their competitor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Misappropriation claims target appropriation of the plaintiff's created value (system, timing, collected content) rather than lawful competitive use of independent systems.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication does not necessarily destroy property rights in news
rubrics_metrics.description: The rule by which literary property is supposed to cease upon an unrestricted publication, without copyright, is entirely inapplicable to the conditions which make and support the status of news as property... the common law rights not being superseded by statute, still persist.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Unlike literary works where publication may extinguish certain rights, news (particularly time-sensitive commercial news) can retain common-law property protection despite public dissemination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Doctrine of restriction by implication preserves rights after publication
rubrics_metrics.description: The doctrine of loss of property rights by publication in literary property is based upon a conception of voluntary dedication to the public. Where a restriction is made either expressly or by implication, the owner's rights continue, however broad and unlimited the publication may otherwise be.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the conditions of business or the circumstances of distribution imply limits on downstream use (e.g., not for republication/sale in competition), courts will treat publication as non-dedication and will preserve the owner’s rights.

rubrics_metrics.name: Implied restriction focuses on intended use, not mere access
rubrics_metrics.description: The real restriction... is the one which is implied against the use to which the readers may put the ticker news. Every adult man can see the items if he wants to, but nobody is intended to be given any right to take them off the blackboard for commercial sale as news.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Access or public display alone does not authorize appropriation for commercial resale; courts look at the intended/authorized use by recipients.

rubrics_metrics.name: General vs limited publication — display doesn't authorize appropriation
rubrics_metrics.description: The merchant displays his goods in windows... but this does not authorize his competitors or others to appropriate the property so displayed without compensation nor does it in any way deprive the owner of his right of protection to all of his property rights therein.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Public exhibition or posting (e.g., ticker, blackboard, bulletin) can be a limited dedication; it does not necessarily forfeit the owner's exclusive commercial rights to exploit that material.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use intended determines when taking is wrongful (notes vs reproduction)
rubrics_metrics.description: If the spectator desires, there is no reason why he should not be permitted to take notes for any fair purpose... It is the use intended to be made of that which is learned which affords just ground of complaint... It is the use of it for representation which operates to deprive the author of his rights.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Courts distinguish harmless private uses (notes, memory) from uses intended to reproduce/compete commercially; only the latter will be enjoined as misappropriation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Owner may make limited or partial dedication reserving other rights
rubrics_metrics.description: The owner of a dramatic or musical composition may... make a limited or partial dedication of it, and when his act of dedication is of such a character as to show unmistakably that he does not intend to abandon all right, but simply to give the public the right to have a limited use of his property, or to use it in a particular way, and to reserve to himself whatever is not plainly given, the public acquire the right to use his property to the extent of his dedication, but nothing more.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where dedication is limited (expressly or impliedly), the public only acquires the limited right granted; any use beyond that scope is a violation of reserved rights and may be enjoined.

rubrics_metrics.name: News is not literary property and practical limits on copyrightability
rubrics_metrics.description: All these questions are immaterial, however, because it is so well settled and so plainly obvious that news is not literary property... That news such as involved in the case at bar cannot be copyrighted is apparent from the practical impossibility, for instance, of meeting the requirement of the statute for the filing of two copies or titles of the thousands of dispatches which are sent every day.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because news disbursements are continuous and voluminous, statutory copyright mechanisms are impractical; protection must instead rest on common-law misappropriation and equitable principles tailored to the business realities of news distribution.
